title: Best Dehumidifier for Springtails (2026): Dry Them Out
dek: Springtails can't survive in dry air, so the right dehumidifier in the right spot does more than any spray.
description: The best dehumidifier for springtails in basements, crawl spaces and bathrooms, plus the humidity target and moisture fixes that make them disappear.
intro: If tiny gray specks are hopping across your bathtub, basement slab or windowsill, a **dehumidifier for springtails** is the most effective tool you can buy. Springtails breathe and take in water through their skin, so they dry out fast in air below about 50% relative humidity, and the mold they feed on stops growing in the same conditions. For most homes, our top pick is the **Midea 50-Pint with Pump**: it has the capacity for a damp basement and a built-in pump, so it can run day and night without stopping on a full tank.

This guide is for anyone seeing springtails indoors, especially in a basement, crawl space, bathroom or laundry room. Three things matter most: **put the unit where the moisture is** (usually below the floor you see the bugs on), **choose drainage that keeps it running around the clock**, and **check your progress with a hygrometer**. Springtails are harmless nuisances, not a structural threat, but they're a reliable sign that something in your house is staying damp.

blocks.text: Springtails eat mold, fungi, algae and decaying plant matter. When a space stays above about 60% humidity, that food supply grows on damp wood, grout, soil and cardboard. Bring the air below 50% and you cut off both their water and their meals at the same time.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for springtails

blocks.text: We don't run a test lab. We compare DOE 2019 and manufacturer capacity ratings, ENERGY STAR listings, owner's manuals and CPSC recall records, then read owner reviews for the patterns that matter here: does the unit run for weeks without fuss, does the drainage keep up, and does it keep working in a cool basement?

Because springtails usually come from one wet zone (a basement, a crawl space, a bathroom), we chose one strong pick for each zone plus a sensor to confirm the job is done. Every card is a verified Amazon listing.

sections.heading: How to choose a dehumidifier for springtails

items.label: Target the source, not the sighting
items.text: Springtails on the first floor often come from a damp crawl space or basement below. Put your main unit there, and add a small one only where a single room stays wet.

items.label: Size for a damp space, not a dry one
items.text: A space with springtails is wetter than average, so size up. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) has the math.
sub: Basement up to about 1,500 sq ft: 35–50 pints
Larger or musty basement: 50 pints with a pump
Crawl space: a dedicated crawl-space unit

items.label: Drainage that runs 24/7
items.text: Plan on running the unit around the clock for several weeks. A gravity hose to a floor drain or a built-in pump keeps it from stopping on a full bucket. Compare options in our [dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

items.label: Cool-room performance
items.text: Springtail season often lines up with cool, wet spring weather. Auto-defrost keeps a compressor working when a basement drops into the low 60s or below.

items.label: A way to see the number
items.text: A display or app helps, but a separate hygrometer near the floor tells you what the bugs are actually living in.

items.label: Running cost
items.text: ENERGY STAR models remove more water per kilowatt-hour, which adds up over weeks of nonstop running.

sections.heading: Why you have springtails in your house

blocks.text: Springtails don't bite, sting or damage wood, and they don't breed well in dry rooms. If you're seeing lots of them, one of these damp spots is almost always nearby:

items: **Basements and crawl spaces:** damp slabs, sill plates and stored cardboard grow the mold films they eat. A [basement dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) or crawl unit is the core fix.
**Bathrooms and kitchens:** wet grout, slow drips under sinks and mildew around tubs. Fix leaks and run the exhaust fan.
**Houseplants:** overwatered potting soil is a springtail nursery. Let the top inch dry between waterings; a dehumidifier won't dry soil you keep soaking.
**New construction or remodels:** fresh concrete, drywall and lumber release moisture for months, and springtails often appear until materials dry out.
**Mulch and window wells:** thick mulch against the foundation stays wet, and springtails move inside when the outdoors dries up.

blocks.title: Springtails or something else?
blocks.text: Springtails are tiny and flick themselves into the air when disturbed. If you're seeing silver, carrot-shaped insects instead, see our [silverfish dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-silverfish/) guide; long-legged hunters are covered in our [centipede](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-centipedes/) guide.

items: **Find the wet zone.** Check under sinks, around the tub, the basement floor and walls, the sump area, crawl-space vapor barriers and houseplant pots.
**Fix water first.** Repair leaks, clean gutters, pull mulch a few inches back from the foundation and regrade where water pools.
**Clean up the food.** Wipe away mildew, toss moldy cardboard and vacuum up visible springtails.
**Run the dehumidifier continuously.** Set it to 45% or continuous mode with a hose or pump until a hygrometer reads under 50% for at least a week.
**Then let the humidistat hold it.** Switch to a 45–50% setpoint and leave it running through the damp season.

blocks.text: Most owners report sightings drop noticeably within a few weeks once a space holds under 50%. If they keep coming back, there's still a moisture source you haven't found. Our guide to [whether a dehumidifier helps with mold](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-help-with-mold/) explains when you need cleanup beyond drying the air.

items: **Springtails in a basement with no floor drain:** the Midea 50-Pint with Pump.
**Springtails upstairs and a crawl space below:** the Aprilaire E070, set up as a permanent crawl-space unit.
**A basement with a floor drain and a tight budget:** the Keystone 50-Pint on a gravity hose.
**Springtails in the tub, shower or laundry room:** the Whirlpool 25-Pint plus a working exhaust fan.
**Any of the above:** add the Govee H5179 so you know when the space is truly dry.

blocks.text: Springtails are a moisture problem wearing a bug costume. Fix the leaks and drainage, then run a dehumidifier where the dampness lives until the space holds below 50%. The Midea 50-Pint with Pump is the best all-around choice for basements, the Aprilaire E070 dries crawl spaces at the source, the Keystone is the value pick, the Whirlpool 25-Pint handles bathrooms, and a Govee hygrometer proves it's working. If other moisture pests are showing up too, our [flea](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-fleas/) guide covers the same humidity strategy for a different bug.

faqs.q: Does a dehumidifier get rid of springtails?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. Springtails need damp air and the mold that grows in it, so holding a space below about 50% humidity dries them out and cuts off their food. It works best alongside fixing leaks, drainage and overwatered plants.

There's no single cutoff, but springtails struggle in air below about 50% relative humidity and can't build large populations there. Aim for 45–50% in the affected space and confirm it with a hygrometer placed near the floor.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for springtails in a basement?
faqs.a: A 50-pint unit with continuous drainage. The Midea 50-Pint with Pump is our top pick because it can run nonstop without a floor drain; the Keystone 50-Pint is the value choice if you have one.

faqs.q: Why do I have springtails in my bathroom?
faqs.a: Bathrooms stay humid after showers, and wet grout, caulk and small leaks grow the mildew springtails eat. Run the exhaust fan for 20–30 minutes after showering, fix drips and use a small dehumidifier if the room stays damp.

faqs.q: Are springtails a sign of mold?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Springtails feed on mold and fungi, so a large population usually means there's mold growth or constant dampness nearby, even if you can't see it. Track down the moisture source as well as the bugs.

faqs.q: How long should I run a dehumidifier for springtails?
faqs.a: Continuously for the first few weeks, until the space holds below 50% for at least a week. After that, set the humidistat to 45–50% and let it cycle on its own through the damp season.
